title: What is the Accenture Strategy interview process, and how should you prepare?
description: How Accenture's strategy and consulting roles tend to hire: HR screens, behavioural and case interviews with a technology angle, and a final senior…
hook: Accenture is best known for technology, but it also hires strategy consultants, and its strategy interviews include real case work. Candidates often describe them as more conversational than MBB, with a technology flavour.
body:
What candidates commonly report

  • An initial recruiter or HR conversation about your background and interest in Accenture.
  • Behavioural and case interviews, often paired in a round: one case, one behavioural.
  • A final conversation with a senior leader, such as a managing director, which may be more of a discussion than a formal case.

The exact steps vary widely by country, practice and level, so ask your recruiter.

The technology angle

Because so much of Accenture's work involves technology, expect cases that touch digital transformation, data, cloud or automation. You do not need to be technical, but you should be able to talk sensibly about how technology changes a business: costs, customer experience, speed and risk.

How to prepare

  • Practise standard cases (profitability, market entry, cost reduction), then add one or two technology-flavoured ones.
  • Read a little about current technology trends in the industry you are interviewing for.
  • Prepare a clear answer to why Accenture, linked to the kind of work it does.

Sources

  • StrategyCase: Big 4 case interviews (Accenture section)
  • Glassdoor: Accenture strategy interview reviews

Checked November 2026. Processes change by office and year, so always confirm with the firm's own careers page and your recruiter.

Connect a strategic answer to implementation

Consider a retailer deciding whether to introduce AI-supported customer service. First clarify the objective: lower cost, faster response, better quality, or a combination. Estimate the economic opportunity, identify which enquiry types can be automated reliably, and consider how existing systems and teams would change.

Suppose 500,000 routine enquiries cost £4 each today and an automated workflow can resolve 60% of them at a variable cost of £0.50. The gross yearly saving on those resolved enquiries is £1.05 million: 300,000 × (£4 − £0.50). That is before development, monitoring, failure-handling, escalations and the cost of any deterioration in quality. A good recommendation weighs those issues rather than extrapolating the headline saving across all contacts.

Prepare to discuss not only what the client should do but how to test and deliver it: a limited pilot, success metrics, employee training and a rollback plan. The precise interview sequence for Accenture Strategy varies by geography and level, so use your recruiter invitation to decide whether to prioritise cases, personal stories, a presentation or technical discussion.
